requiredFindings.title: The ordering hazard treats a later-generation floor as F22
requiredFindings.failureScenario: Owner step 3 reports unknown-quarantine-condition for k > t only when stableH, the two tails agree, and H.lastSeq >= k. Otherwise the standing is unavailable-busy. covers() in recovery_capture.rs is true for every floor in a later generation. Case C uses that predicate for records of a closed generation, which is the right anchor rule. The F43 arm (query.seq > t) uses it too, and decide then reports FloorRegression with offending None. A lawful open-successor floor at (G+1, 0, null) passes floor_against as Unchanged and skips floorOk because seq is 0. A query above the closed generation's tail therefore quarantines a healthy carrier. H.lastSeq is 0, so the owner standing is UnavailableBusy. A same-generation floor above that generation's tail is already FloorRegression at step 14, with the floor digest; the F43 test plants s.seq+1 and takes that path. Keep covers() for case C. In the k > t arm, covers is true only when the floor generation equals the requested generation and floor.seq >= query.seq. Carry offending(h1) on Verdict::Hazard and copy it into UnknownQuarantineCondition.offending. A stable case-1 COMMITTED 0 with floor (G+1, 0, null) and a query sequence above the closed generation's tail expects UnavailableBusy.

requiredFindings.title: The closure chain sums TERMINAL rows
requiredFindings.failureScenario: Call 12 closes a generation when its last row is TERMINAL, the way committed_tail reads the predecessor: the last row below the newest must be TERMINAL in the previous generation. current_view instead requires every generation from g through the newest to exist and SUM(record_type='TERMINAL' AND grantGeneration < newest) == span. The sum counts rows. A generation whose last row is not TERMINAL still adds 1 when an earlier row is TERMINAL, and committed_tail never looks past newest-1. The requested generation's own last row can be TERMINAL, and a joining SEAL in g with an OK witness on the open newest generation confirms. One such carrier is generation 1 closed on its last row, generation 2 holding a TERMINAL followed by a non-terminal row, generation 3 closed on its last row, and generation 4 open at a matching witness and floor: span 3 and the sum 3. gj3_append_laws aborts that insert, and plant() drops the trigger to put rows in the file; the reader classifies the bytes. Count generations in [g, newest) whose maximum-seq row is TERMINAL and require that count to equal newest-g. A missing generation and a generation whose last row is not TERMINAL both fail, and an extra TERMINAL does not close another generation. The intermediate case above expects ProtocolViolation. The missing-generation test stays.
